Add the no-worker-identifiers rule and its email check (#292)

Add the adopter-owned rule under .claude/rules/external/ that bars any
worker email address, account identifier, seat label, or other
third-party identifier from every public or potentially public
surface, and link it from the Adopted governance section of
.claude/CLAUDE.md.

Add tools/test-no-worker-identifiers.py, which reads the raw bytes of
every regular file that git ls-files lists and the name of every path
it lists, and takes every candidate address around every at sign, so
an exempt candidate cannot hide another, with work that grows linearly
with the file. 2 exemptions, each tested on a candidate folded to lower
case, so each holds in any letter case: (1) the candidate is exactly
the maintainer's own email address; (2) the domain of the candidate is
reserved for documentation: its last label is invalid, test, or
example, or it is, or ends with a dot and then, example.com,
example.org, or example.net. An at sign passes only when every
candidate that the scan reads at it is exempt, under either
exemption, or when it lies in a file on a line that the reviewed
exact-line allowlist holds for that file. So, off such a line, an
address passes only when each shorter domain that it holds, ending
after 2 or more letters that follow a dot, gives an exempt candidate
as well. 1 exact-line allowlist entry covers the URL-userinfo fixture
in tools/test-release-links.py; a stale entry fails.

A failure names the file, the line number, and a digest of the match,
never the matched text or the line. A path whose name holds a match is
named in each of its failures only by a digest of the path name; any
other path name is printed with each character that is not printable,
such as a line feed, a carriage return, or the escape byte of a
terminal escape sequence, and each backslash written as a backslash
escape, so each failure is 1 line. A red run prints every failure in
full, 1 to a line after a count, never through a list comparison that
unittest shortens. A failed git call, a git that cannot start, an
empty listing, a missing file, and an unreadable file are failures,
never a skip, and each gives only a fixed category with the exit code
of git or the errno name or type of the error, never a diagnostic of
git, the message of an exception, the error text of the system, or the
path of the repository or of git; a missing or unreadable file is
named by its repository path, or, when its path name holds a match,
only by a digest of the path name, as every failure names its file.
Each caught example in the suite is assembled at run time, so its
source holds no matchable text.

Run the suite as a named step of the Orchestration registry workflow,
name it in the header of that workflow, mirror it in
tools/run_all_checks.sh, and record the new sha256 of that script in
tools/test-run-all-checks.py, which pins it.

Residual: the check covers the email class only. A seat label, a bare
account handle, or a numeric account identifier passes it, because a
committed pattern that names a real label would itself publish the
label; those forms rest on the rule, on the standing line that every
QA and drafting brief carries, and on any scan the maintainer keeps
outside the repository. An address split across lines, assembled by
code, or written with the word "at" passes. An untracked file, the
target of a tracked symbolic link, and the content of a submodule are
not read. An address inside compressed or encoded binary content
passes, since the scan neither decompresses nor decodes, unless that
content holds the address as it is. An at sign outside ASCII, such as
the fullwidth or the small commercial at sign, passes, and so does an
at sign written as an HTML character reference, such as the decimal or
the named form, percent-encoded, as a backslash escape, such as \x40,
\100, or the JSON or JavaScript escape of U+0040, or as
quoted-printable =40. An address with a space right after the at sign
passes, since its domain run is then empty. An address whose local
part ends, right before the at sign, in a byte that the local part
does not name, such as a letter outside ASCII, a tilde, an exclamation
mark, or an apostrophe, passes, since its local part is then empty. An
address with a quoted local part, with a domain written with letters
outside ASCII or as a literal in square brackets, with an underscore in
its domain, with a zero-width space or a soft hyphen inside its domain,
or with a dot of its domain written as an
HTML character reference or percent-encoded, can pass. A surface that
is not a file in this tree, such as a pull request title, description,
or comment, is not reached, and tools/check-pr-text.py carries no
identifier pattern today. The suite pins each form of text that passes
with its own subtest, named for the form, apart from compressed or
encoded content, which has its own case, and each place that is not
read with its own case. The digest of a match or of a path name lets
a reader who already holds a guess of the address confirm the guess.
A path name is held back only from the output of the suite: git and
other steps that list files can still print it. On a red run, unittest
also prints a traceback for each failed case, which holds the absolute
path of the suite file in the checkout, and a failed self-check can
print the values that it compared, the path of its temporary folder
among them, so a checkout path or a temporary folder path that holds
an address reaches the CI log. A label that leaked into the history of
an older pull request and was removed later is held for the maintainer
and is out of scope for the rule's enforcement.

Accepted false failures: a legitimate new third-party address is
caught and needs a maintainer decision; email-shaped text that is no
address is caught and is reworded to a reserved documentation domain,
or is added to the allowlist after review; a fixture address at a
reserved domain that also holds a shorter domain that is not reserved,
such as 1 at mail.corp.example.com or 1 that appends the label example
to an ordinary domain, is caught and is reworded to a reserved domain
with no such shorter domain; and an action pinned to a version tag in
which a dot is followed directly by 2 or more letters, such as
v1.2.3-alpha.beta.1 or v2.0.0-rc.ab, is caught, since a domain then
ends after those letters, unless every domain that the tag ends is
exempt, as in v1.2.3-pre.test.1, whose letters form a reserved last
label, or v1.0.0-rc.example.com, while a tag whose every dot is
followed by a digit, such as v1.2.3-rc.1, passes.
